scope: Selected working-eval qualification cases only. Original questions remain the scoring reference; no workbook edits.

proposals.proposal: Remove the repeated question asking for the terminating SKU.
Remove the storage yes/no question and retain the lookup-trigger question.
Remove the question asking whether live traffic is needed.
Ask whether those outlets are visited in one route and must be submitted together. Do not assume the daily outlet count is a per-request waypoint count.
Remove the repeated language question; retain workload and storage confirmation because volumes are missing and may store is uncertain.

excerpts: only want reverse-geocoded addresses when the location is known to street-address (rooftop) precision
they need an address broken into elements
proposals.proposal: Remove repeated precision and breakdown confirmations. If provider selection is needed, ask which providers to evaluate without presupposing Google and Nominatim.
Compare both requested scenarios instead of asking the customer to choose one.
Obtain billing units from provider documentation. Ask for monthly and peak matrix request frequency, then normalize equivalent workloads.

implementation_observations_not_label_ed.observation: A daily outlet count does not establish one route or one request. Existing inference may suppress a legitimate route-size question. No change included in this validation-repair comparison.
The customer already places matrix usage in India, but the candidate asks again for usage geography together with billing country. Review operating-region to usage-geography fact binding separately.
The matched yes/no storage question does not independently demonstrate retention-duration or licensing-rights coverage.

On reopen, both before and after ask for the map provider again after Mapbox was supplied. Answered state uses current_provider while pending_reply uses provider. Preservation passes because both versions share this existing alias-binding defect; it does not prove the follow-up is correct.
